findings.passage: Her outward answers cover the most ground: a hard scene, a "crazy" industry, a world out of control. Her inward answers cluster around two questions: whether she deserves her place as two stars' daughter, and whether people will like her strange taste.
findings.problem: The first of the two observations that tip the read toward the Six counts where she goes for steadiness, but the article never shows the self-talk she uses in several of the same interviews: 'I may feel this way, but I have to go to work tomorrow' (Vanity Fair 2024, about feeling 'so out of my depth' on Nosferatu), 'Everything is mental. I'm good. I'm chilling' (Portman 2024, on set) and 'I always try to remind myself' (Knightley 2021, before 'trust is so huge'). These are inward steadying moves outside the parentage and taste topics. They do not overturn the narrow Six lean, since the outward move appears alongside them, but leaving them out makes the outward/inward tally look cleaner than the record is. The same tilt shows in the type answer's 'usually steadies through people and structures she trusts' (C37, C124).
findings.acceptance_test: At the next refresh, the 'First, where she goes when she doubts herself' paragraph (or the type section) acknowledges in one sentence, with at least one quoted example, that she also steadies herself with self-talk, and says whether that changes the lean. C124 and C37 record the self-talk instances, and the C107/C127 tallies count self-talk about doubt as inward.
